paragraphs.source_en: Gillenormand’s mobile face was no longer expressive of anything but rough and ineffable good-nature. The grandsire had given way before the grandfather. “Come, see here, speak, tell me about your love affairs, jabber, tell me everything! Sapristi! how stupid young folks are!” “Father—” repeated Marius. The old man’s entire countenance lighted up with indescribable radiance. “Yes, that’s right, call me father, and you’ll see!” There was now something so kind, so gentle, so openhearted, and so paternal in this brusqueness, that Marius, in the sudden transition from discouragement to hope, was stunned and intoxicated by it, as it were.
